Punggol 48

  1. Must see · Punggol

    Coney Island Park (Pulau Serangoon)

    A 133-hectare island off Punggol, once owned by the Aw brothers of Tiger Balm. In 1950 it was sold to a businessman who planned a resort modelled on New York's Coney Island. Since October 2015 a 50-hectare NParks park has kept it deliberately rustic: casuarina woods, a 2.5 km car-free trail, hidden beaches and bridges at both ends to the mainland.

    Look for Open 7am–7pm, free

    Coney Island, Punggol, Singapore (West entrance off Punggol Promenade / East entrance off Pasir Ris side; to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NParks (National Parks Board), Little Day Out, City Nomads (Singapore city guide), TheSmartLocal

  2. Must see · Punggol

    Punggol Beach Massacre Site

    A National Heritage Board historic site. On 23 February 1942, during the Japanese Sook Ching operation, a Hojo Kempei firing squad killed some 300–400 Chinese civilians on the Punggol foreshore. Human remains turned up in the sand in 1977 and 1997. An NHB marker set up in 1995, for the 50th anniversary of the end of WWII, records the killings.

    Look for Open-air memorial marker, free

    Punggol Point foreshore (Punggol Point Park), Punggol, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), SG101, National Heritage Board, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Punggol

    Punggol Waterway Park

    The 4.2-km park along Singapore's longest man-made waterway, in four themed zones (Nature Cove, Recreation Zone, Heritage Zone on Old Punggol Road, Green Gallery) linked by five photogenic bridges — the dome-shaped Jewel Bridge for sunsets over the Punggol and Serangoon reservoirs, the snaking red Sunrise Bridge at the eastern Sunrise Gateway, plus the Wave, Adventure and Kelong bridges. Otters are regulars.

    Your guide’s note Free; best at sunrise (east) and sunset (Jewel Bridge, west)

    Punggol Waterway (Sentul Crescent / Punggol Central), Punggol, Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Housing & Development Board (heritage studies), TheSmartLocal, SilverStreak (Singapore lifestyle guide)

  4. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Punggol

    Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge (One Punggol)

    Punggol branch of a Teochew fish-porridge stall founded in 1962 and on the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand list every year since 2021. Known for a light, clean, sweet-savoury broth and fresh fish slices; the original is at Newton Food Centre.

    One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-19, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Michelin Guide, Eatbook.sg, Her World Singapore

  5. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Punggol

    Whisk & Paddle

    The Punggol waterfront café that set the template for the estate's brunch scene: all-day breakfast plates (eggs Benedict, bacon-and-egg waffles) in a house by Tebing Lane — named across Lady Iron Chef, Honeycombers and Eatbook's Punggol guides.

    10 Tebing Lane, Singapore 828836

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, ladyironchef (Brad Lau), The Honeycombers Singapore, Time Out Singapore, Seth Lui

  6. Worth the detour · Punggol

    Punggol Regional Library

    NLB's five-storey regional library in the One Punggol hub (opened in stages Jan-Apr 2023), built as an inclusive library with interactive exhibits, tech zones and a free MakeIT maker space for 3D printing, digital cutting and robotics.

    Look for Public library; free

    One Punggol, 1 Punggol Drive, #01-12, Singapore 828629

    Recommended by National Library Board, Wikipedia, TheSmartLocal, Little Day Out

  7. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Punggol

    Eng Kee Chicken Wings (One Punggol)

    The beloved wing stall's sixth outlet: wings marinated through, coated in a light, crunchy batter and fried super-crisp and juicy, about $1.70 each — the One Punggol stall that Seth Lui, Her World, Daniel Food Diary and Mothership all name.

    One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-34, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore, Daniel Food Diary, Mothership

  8. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Punggol

    Anna's Sourdough (Punggol)

    A sourdough-centric bakery-café that turned one starter into loaves, toasties, soups, pastas and pizzas when it opened in Punggol in Oct 2022 — covered by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere and Time Out, and on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol list.

    Punggol, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, Time Out Singapore

  9. Worth the detour · Punggol

    Punggol Point Park

    A seafront park at the northern tip of Punggol, opened on 20 November 2011 at the old Punggol Point fishing-village beach. People come for the sunset over the Strait of Johor, the jetty views across to Malaysia, and the WWII Sook Ching memorial on its foreshore.

    Look for Open 24h, free

    Punggol Point Road, Punggol, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Time Out Singapore, TheSmartLocal

  10. Worth the detour · Punggol

    Punggol Digital District (SIT Punggol Campus)

    Singapore's first 'enterprise district' (~50 ha, phase 1 opened from Q3 2024), marketed as Singapore's "Silicon Valley" and built around the Singapore Institute of Technology's new Punggol campus (classes from Sept 2024); the BCA Green Mark Platinum campus runs on 20,000+ sensors and smart lamp-posts. Campus Heart houses the SIT Visitor Gallery.

    Look for SIT Visitor Gallery; pair with Punggol Coast Hawker Centre

    Punggol Coast, Punggol Way, Singapore (beside Punggol Coast MRT)

    Recommended by Wikipedia, JTC Corporation, Monocle

  11. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Punggol

    Izakaya 95 (Punggol Settlement)

    A no-frills izakaya hidden on the second storey of The Punggol Settlement, where Japanese bar grub comes with a waterfront sunset — a fixture on Punggol food guides from Lady Iron Chef (2018) to Eatbook's current 30-best list.

    500 New Punggol Road, #02-05, The Punggol Settlement, Singapore 828617

  12. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Punggol

    Warabimochi Kamakura (Waterway Point)

    The viral Kamakura warabimochi specialist (snaking queues at its 2024 Holland Village debut) opened its first dine-in café here in Oct 2024, with café-only warabimochi drinks, a kuromitsu soft serve dusted with kinako and a warabimochi-and-hot-matcha set — covered by Time Out, Mothership and Eatbook.

    Waterway Point West Wing #01-72/73, 83 Punggol Central, Singapore 828761

  13. Worth the detour · Punggol

    Matilda House

    One of Singapore's oldest houses: a 1902 single-storey tropical bungalow built for Alexander Cashin and named for his mother Josephine Matilda — the Cashins being the Eurasian family whose patriarch became Singapore's first Eurasian millionaire. Conserved by URA in Feb 2000 and restored (façade and interior) as the clubhouse of the 'A Treasure Trove' condominium in 2015; view from Punggol Walk.

    Look for Conserved 1902 bungalow; condo clubhouse — exterior view only

    78 Punggol Walk, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Urban Redevelopment Authority

  23. Deep cut · Punggol

    Masjid Al-Islah

    Punggol's only mosque (2015, capacity 4,000), designed by Formwerkz Architects as an 'open mosque': a porous, naturally ventilated village cluster of prayer hall, school and offices around landscaped courts — widely published as a model of contemporary Singapore mosque architecture.

    Look for Visitors welcome outside prayer times; dress modestly

    30 Punggol Field, Singapore 828812

    Recommended by Wikipedia, ArchNet (mit / Aga Khan Trust for Culture), Architizer

  24. Deep cut · Punggol

    Oasis Terraces

    HDB's new-generation neighbourhood centre on the Punggol Waterway (opened 2018–19), designed by Serie Architects with Multiply Architects as a stepped garden of terraces cascading to the water, with a rooftop community garden and polyclinic — published internationally by Dezeen and designboom. Houses Lao Jiang Superior Soup and Rise & Grind.

    Look for Free; climb the terraces to the rooftop garden for waterway views

    681 Punggol Drive, Singapore 820681

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Dezeen, designboom

    Singapore's round-the-clock prawning pond by the Punggol riverside: six ponds under a thatched, lantern-hung roof, rods and bait included, barbecue pits and salt to grill your catch on the spot, and a cheap beer garden — Time Out's Punggol pick, also in TheSmartLocal's and Honeycombers' prawning guides.

  28. Deep cut · Punggol

    Waterway Point

    Punggol's main mall, with more than 200 stores, on the banks of Punggol Waterway next to the MRT. It is the town's main food cluster, covered in its own Eatbook food guide, and the jumping-off point for the waterway park.

    Waterway Point, beside Punggol MRT/Punggol Waterway, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by TheSmartLocal, Eatbook.sg

  29. Deep cut · Punggol

    Punggol Point Jetty

    A long-standing, iconic jetty at Punggol Point — the coast of kelongs such as the 1969 Sea Palace kelong restaurant-cum-nightclub on stilts that made Punggol Point a seafood-and-leisure destination; NHB names Punggol Jetty among Punggol's heritage landmarks. Views to Pulau Ubin and the Johor Strait.

    Look for Free; sunset; combine with Punggol Point Park

    Punggol Point Park, end of Punggol Point Road, Punggol, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

  30. Deep cut · Punggol

    Treelodge@Punggol

    HDB's first eco-precinct (2010): seven 16-storey blocks with rainwater harvesting, solar-powered common areas, a wind-channelling 'eco-deck' and a community garden — the first public-housing project to win the Green Mark Platinum award, and the pilot for the Punggol eco-town.

    Look for Residential estate — view from Punggol Drive; the eco-deck and garden are for residents

    Punggol Road / Punggol Drive / Punggol Place, Punggol, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Housing & Development Board (heritage studies)

  31. Deep cut · Punggol

    Punggol Waterway Terraces

    Singapore's first waterfront public housing, won in an international HDB design competition by Group8asia with Aedas: stepped blocks that echo Asian rice terraces, sky terraces and roof gardens cascading down to the waterway (Waterway Terraces II is Green Mark Platinum) — published by designboom and awarded at the RTF Sustainability Awards 2016.

    Look for Best seen from the Punggol Waterway promenade near Sumang

    Punggol Walk / Punggol Way / Sumang Link, along Punggol Waterway, Singapore

    Recommended by designboom, Rethinking The Future (RTF) Awards

  48. Closed — kept for the record · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Punggol

    Ponggol Seafood — CLOSED

The seafood restaurant that carried the old 'Ponggol' spelling and the memory of the kelong-era Punggol seafood strip — in business since 1965, famous for chilli crab, lala bee hoon and mee goreng (Honeycombers) — quietly shut after 55 years (Seth Lui).
